Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Archer + Whistic onboarding + evidence delegation

Hi Tessa,

We're kicking off security onboarding for Redwood as part of our Q3 vendor intake. Two asks up front:

1) Can you confirm your preferred workflow for portal invites (Archer and Whistic)? We prefer to grant read-only service accounts rather than long-lived user invites.

2) We need to understand how Redwood prefers evidence custody/delegation for SIG/CAIQ artifacts — e.g., do you accept vendor-hosted evidence in Whistic, or do you require files delivered to our S3 and signed manifests?

I've attached a partial SIG export to speed things up (Kirby_SIG_partial.xlsx). We're happy to upload additional artifacts to a temporary S3 bucket or grant portal access; your guidance will determine which we do.

Target timeline: portal access this week if possible; evidence package by Friday (6/27).

Thanks,
Sally Hogan
Vendor Risk Manager
Kirby Retail

Attachment: Kirby_SIG_partial.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Sally Hogan <sally.hogan@kirbyretail.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Archer + Whistic onboarding + evidence delegation

Hi Sally — thanks for the export and the timeline. Welcome aboard. A couple quick clarifications so we can route this correctly:

- Scope: Do you want both Archer and Whistic access, or are we onboarding to one portal first? (If Archer only, we can gate Whistic until we map CAIQ fields.)
- Service account model: we prefer a short-lived read-only service account (SAML/OAuth) scoped to the portal inventory and evidence objects.
- Evidence custody: our standard is vendor-hosted portal proof for SIG/CAIQ (Whistic/OneTrust) when possible; where customers require possession proof we can provide signed manifests and a KMS-backed proof-of-possession hash.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aditya — can you confirm technical requirements for our SSO/service account (metadata, required claims, acceptable TTLs)?
2) Sally — if you can grant a Whistic/Archer role "vendor_read_only" to security@redwood.ai that will let us ingest the SIG QA and attach our evaluation notes.
3) I'll send a short delegation playbook and our SSO guide.

If we get portal access today, we'll do a light inventory and call out any missing CAIQ items that block SOC2 evidence mapping.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Success — Security Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Sally Hogan <sally.hogan@kirbyretail.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Archer + Whistic onboarding + evidence delegation

Hi all — quick tech details so we don't hit any surprises during ingestion: 

- SSO/service account: We can accept either SAML (IdP-initiated) or an OAuth2 client credential flow. For SAML we need the metadata XML and 2 attributes: email (NameID) and org_role. For OAuth2 we need client_id/client_secret rotation window and a JWKS endpoint if you support JWT assertions.
- Permissions: read-only at portal inventory + proof objects. No write permissions.
- TTLs: short-lived tokens preferred (<= 12 hours). If you must provide a long-lived API key, we'll wrap it in our ephemeral credential store and rotate on 24h cycle.
- Evidence retrieval: if you're providing signed artifacts to our S3, please sign manifests with your KMS key (key id + signature) so we can validate provenance. We can also accept Whistic shared links, but we cannot rely on user accounts that require MFA prompts during automated ingestion.

I'll attach two quick references: redwood_sso_integration_guide.pdf and delegation-playbook.md. They include the exact claim names and the minimal IAM policy we need.

Let me know if your SSO team needs to loop in our platform-infra alias (platform-infra@redwood.ai) — that speeds certificate exchange.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Security Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sso_integration_guide.pdf (15 pages), delegation-playbook.md (4KB)
